ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, s. 462.31; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 21.1 (for federal corporate general partners). Provincial: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, arts. 15–23 and 33.1–33.7 (beneficial owners); Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c. CCQ-1991, arts. 2235–2247 (limited partnership formation); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing/Corporate Status for each non-resident corporate general partner and any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry authority in the foreign jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the relevant foreign competent authority (or consular legalization where the issuing state is not an Apostille Convention party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and proof of residential address for each general partner and every beneficial owner holding a 25% or greater interest
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or other competent attesting authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, together with notarized certification of the signatory's capacity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing a Quebec-domiciled representative/agent for service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the foreign general partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the signature and authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of the partnership agreement, corporate resolutions, and all non-French corporate records relied upon for registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator accredited by the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec (OTTIAQ) or another REQ-recognized translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No separate apostille; the translation must be attached to the original notarized/apostilled underlying document, and the translator's seal and certification appear on the translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and UBOs against (i) FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) definitions and guidance, (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the Canadian Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, (iv) the Freezing Assets of Corrupted Foreign Officials Regulations, (v) OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List as prudent practice for USD wire transactions, and (vi) domestic Quebec policing and regulatory enforcement databases. For this medium-risk passive SPV, the protocol further requires risk-based enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation for any UBO holding 25% or more, and written sign-off by the compliance officer prior to formation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under s. 51 of the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), every enterprise established in Quebec must have its legal name (raison sociale) in French. A limited partnership must use a French form such as 'Société en commandite' (S.E.C.) or 'S.E.C.' as the legal suffix. Non-French names are permitted only with a valid exception (e.g., recognized trademark, proper name, international title) or upon authorization from the Office québécois de la langue française. Names originating in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet in the form intended for daily commercial use in Quebec.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Securities Dealer / Courtier en valeurs mobilières
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises du Québec rejects a requested name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registration Service within 30 days of written notice, including revised name options and arguments demonstrating conformity with French-language and public-order rules. A reissued authorization may be obtained by paying a new reservation fee; reservations can be extended by filing a new application before expiry. If the Registrar upholds the refusal, the applicant may proceed to judicial review before the Court of Québec by filing an application against the Registrar within 30 days of the final refusal, pursuant to arts. 42–44 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-agent address is generally accepted for a passive holding SPV in Quebec, provided it is a physical address within Quebec at which the Registrar and process-serving authorities can effectively deliver documents; a P.O. box alone is insufficient. The service provider should not be a shell without a real establishment, and the limited partnership must maintain local records at that address or at another accessible address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: 3–5% annualized probability for a non-regulated intermediate holding entity, absent tax-aggressiveness indicators, related-party financing anomalies, or Quebec annual declaration deficiencies. If the SPV engages in lending, cross-border finance, or claims treaty benefits inconsistent with substance, the inspection probability escalates to over 30% annually.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government name-reservation application and initial name search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule under CQLR c. P-44.1 (approximate CAD 100, converted at 1.30 CAD/USD)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of partnership declaration, partner resolutions, and related formation consents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec notary (Chambre des notaires du Québec member)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff and prevailing market fee for a non-complex LP declaration package in Montreal or Quebec City

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign corporate documents and partnership instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per page/per word for bilingual translation with notarized certification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign public and corporate documents (estimated three documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global Affairs Canada / foreign competent authority / consular service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory authentication fee (CAD 15 per document) plus customary service/courier charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enhanced UBO verification, PEP and sanctions screening, and source-of-funds review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML/KYC compliance service provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee for medium-risk non-routine SPV with non-resident UBOs
Market benchmark for corporate agent/office services including regulatory correspondence handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-border corporate and tax legal review of LP structure, UBO threshold, and treaty access opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External cross-border corporate law firm admitted in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed or hourly professional fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Acquisition of certified copies, courier, notarial photocopying, and incidental administrative costs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party service providers and courier/certification offices

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2242 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 20-24
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar), operating with Revenu Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Registration Declaration) of a société en commandite
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement; no escrow account obligation for Québec limited partnerships.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) SUBSCRIPTION: The board approves the subscription of [General Partner Inc.] as general partner of [Name] Limited Partnership and authorizes execution of the declaration of registration and the partnership agreement. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office in Québec is fixed at [address], and [Attorney] is appointed agent for service of process. (3) OFFICERS: [Name] and [Name] are appointed as authorized officers with full power to sign, file, and certify all statutory registrations. (4) ADMINISTRATION: The officers are authorized to open bank accounts and obtain business numbers. Each resolution is approved and effective upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online portal (Quebec Business Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a compliance name search via the Registraire's 'Nom d'entreprise' service. Submit proposed name for conditional reservation and receive confirmation. No notarization is required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Proposed name and suffix 'société en commandite' / 'Limited Partnership'
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name submission within 30 days incorporating the registry's objections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Partnership Agreement and Registration Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel or notary (optional, for authentication)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) and the declaration of registration identifying the general partner, registered office, and limited partners' contributions. Segregate an address for service and appoint an attorney if the general partner is not resident in Québec.
required_dossiers: Proof of general partner identity/corporate status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the declaration and resubmit with explanatory cover letter if the registrar queries the legal form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Registration with the Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (filing window and e-services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed declaration of registration through the online 'E-Certificate of registration' service or at the service counter. Pay the government fee using credit card or Interac. The registrar will acknowledge receipt and issue a numbered or named registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notice of deficiency is issued, file a corrective declaration and supporting evidence within the delay prescribed; a late registration fee may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, retrieve the 'Attestation d'immatriculation'. Enroll with Revenu Québec for a Québec enterprise number and, where applicable, register for GST/QST accounts. A passive dividend-holding SPV may request a non-resident or exempt status where eligible.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the attestation data by filing a declaration of modification with supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (continuing compliance window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the declaration lists all general partners and mandatory information. Appoint a registered agent for service if required. Maintain internal registers and delegate any future filings to authorized officers. Submit annual declaration (déclaration de mise à jour) within 60 days of each anniversary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is late, file it with the prescribed late fee and avoid loss of registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None — the entity undertakes no industrial or physical production in Québec.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating permit required for passive holding of subsidiary shares.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not applicable — no project, construction, or discharge-triggering activity under the Québec Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or air emission sources; SPV holds only financial assets, so no discharge limits apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — no employees, workplace, or fire-risk installations; a virtual registered office does not require civil defense or structural occupancy certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online portal at www.canada.ca (federal GST/HST accounts and Business Number/BN issuer); Quebec provincial counterpart: Revenu Québec (RQ) — Quebec Sales Tax (QST) account and Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ) issued via the Registraire des entreprises du Québec at revenuquebec.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-incorporated Canadian limited partnership (or non-resident owning an LP): (1) determine whether the partnership carries on business or is required to collect GST/HST in Canada; (2) apply through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) for a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account, using Form RC1 or the online electronic application, providing legal name, fiscal period, business activity (ISIC 6420 / NAICS 551112 passive share holding), mailing address, and the operating business identification of each general partner; (3) register the extra-provincial limited partnership with the Quebec enterprise registrar to obtain the NEQ and QST account; (4) where the partnership has no Canadian resident partner, file Form RC59 (Business Number request for non-resident) and appoint an authorized representative under the CRA electronic services; (5) use the BN for T5013 partnership information return filings and the QST number for TP-600R-QC and provincial remittances; (6) designate a service address in Canada for records; if no taxable supplies are made, registration is not compulsory, but an optional QST holding-entity election may be filed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Canadian domestic law; the limited partnership is statutorily transparent for income tax purposes (ITA s. 96, subdivision j). Available elections/mechanisms: (i) statutory characterization as a 'Canadian partnership' under ITA s. 102, maintained by ensuring all partners are Canadian residents, preserving Part I taxation and treaty access; (ii) functional-currency election under ITA s. 261 to compute Canadian tax liabilities in US dollars; (iii) optional QST registration / holding-entity election under s. 165.1 Quebec Sales Tax Act (QSTA) for QST input-tax refund recovery; (iv) GST/HST joint election under ETA s. 273 for inter-company registrant references; (v) hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.5, 18.6, 20.26, 20.27 effective July 1, 2022) are statutorily prescribed rather than elective, with prescribed information-return documentation for importer mismatch relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT-style goods and services tax) plus Quebec QST (provincial VAT), separately filed with CRA and Revenu Québec; the combined Quebec headline rate is 14.975% (5% GST + 9.975% QST).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies (other than zero-rated) made in Canada over a calendar quarter and the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 240(1)); identical CAD 30,000 threshold under the Quebec Sales Tax Act for QST registration; a pure equity holding SPV earning only dividends has no taxable supplies and is not required to register unless it elects or supplies management services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based e-invoicing clearance is currently in force at CRA or Revenu Québec for B2B supplies. Minimum fiscal documentation obligations include keeping full, sequential, and tamper-proof records of invoices and receipts; GST/HST/QST returns are filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE/EFILE; Revenu Québec online services) on periodic cycles. Canada and Quebec are aligned with the Pan-Canadian Peppol-based B2B e-invoicing framework; Quebec has announced a future transactional data reporting and B2B e-invoicing mandate but it is not yet enacted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated where the supplier ships or delivers tangible property to a destination outside Canada and exports it as soon after shipment as is reasonable (ETA Sch. VI Part V ss. 1, 2, 10, 26); services: zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident not registered under Part IX and not for consumption in Canada (ETA Sch. VI s. 7); financial services supplied to non-residents may zero-rate only as 'exported financial services' under ETA Sch. VII subject to premium-consideration and foreign-account documentation tests. For ISIC 6420 pure equity holding: dividends and share dispositions are not supplies for GST/HST and therefore are not zero-rated events; intercompany management fees billed to non-resident subsidiaries can qualify for zero-rating if the contract, non-resident status, and place-of-consumption tests are documented; input tax credits are generally unavailable for exempt holding activity, but the QST holding-entity election (s. 165.1 QSTA) permits QST recovery on input costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration (Canada Customs Form B13A or CES/ITS electronic export report) for goods, when the export control or valuation thresholds apply
Commercial Invoice with zero-rating statement and intercompany transfer-pricing documentation
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export movement outside Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / bank FX wire confirmation for the export proceeds

Certificate of Residence of the non-resident purchaser (CRA or Revenu Québec acceptable proof, including reciprocal tax-treaty certifications) and the underlying zero-rated service contract where applicable
Six-year books and records retention schedule including T5013/TP-600R-QC partnership returns and QSTA filings
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating, claw back uncollected GST/QST, and assess arrears interest. Reassessment periods: four years generally, seven years for negligence, and unlimited for misrepresentation or fraud (ETA s. 298, ITA s. 152(4)). False-statement penalties: greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the tax misstated (ETA s. 280) with parallel Quebec penalty provisions; gross-negligence penalties also apply under ETA s. 285; criminal evasion penalties under ETA s. 327 / ITA s. 239 expose the taxpayer to fines up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to five years, with equivalent prosecution powers exercised by Revenu Québec under the Quebec Tax Administration Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) for monetary policy and official published exchange rates; Department of Finance Canada and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for sanctions administration, AML/PF supervision, and foreign-currency transaction reporting; no dedicated exchange-control authority exists in Canada under the Currency Act or the Bank Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. No exchange-control restrictions impede dividend distribution, capital repatriation, or equity injection by a Quebec limited partnership to non-resident partners. The residual compliance burden is documentary and tax-driven: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax or treaty relief, Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency reporting, Investment Canada Act net-benefit review where applicable, and enhanced due diligence for FINTRAC and global-sanctions screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, or prescribed repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters and holding entities may retain foreign-currency balances freely; record-keeping obligations apply under the Income Tax Act and FINTRAC thresholds for currency and virtual-currency transactions exceeding CAD 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. A non-bank fintech EMI, whether Canadian-registered as a money-services business or a foreign digital EMI, may provide supplementary cross-border collections, FX execution, and low-value payment routes; however, it cannot lawfully replace a Schedule 1 bank for capital escrow and treasury settlement in Canada. Any foreign EMI carrying on money-services-business activity in Canada must be registered with FINTRAC and comply with Quebec consumer-protection and money-services rules; account-opening limits, deposit-insurance absence, and enhanced-source-of-funds scrutiny materially reduce viability for passive holding-company structures.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is legally permissible in Canada under FINTRAC customer-identification rules when the depositor obtains reliable third-party verification or a dual-process identity-verification procedure. In practice, tier-1 banks classify passive non-resident Quebec limited partnerships as enhanced risk and require at least one principal, being the general-partner representative, executive director, or authorized compliance contact, to complete a recorded KYC interview. Physical presence at a Quebec branch is not a statutory mandate, but most banks recommend or require a video-call interview, certified corporate filings, and a Canadian-cum-Quebec nexus before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership or a chain of intermediate holding entities without a regulated-parent reference
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate-ownership chart covering every entity, jurisdiction, ownership percentage, and operating function; certified registry extracts for each layer; government-issued identification and proof of residential address for every 25% or greater ultimate beneficial owner; notarized partnership deed; and a declaration of no undisclosed nominees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial-substance shortfall for an ISIC 6420 passive equity-holding SPV with no payroll, physical premises, or active business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investment-management and shareholder-liquidity agreements; audited or reviewed financial statements; board or general-partner resolutions authorizing the account; Registraire des entreprises certificate; forecast of dividend and capital flows; and a treasury business-purpose memorandum linking the Quebec LP to its underlying equity portfolio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire-flow mismatch: high-value inbound equity injection followed by immediate onward disbursement to tax-neutral or lower-tax jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed equity subscription, share-purchase, or loan agreements; source-of-funds statement from the investing parent and investor bank; audited LP statements and bank reference letters; tax opinion confirming treaty eligibility and non-artificiality; and a cash-flow model demonstrating a genuine holding-period and distribution plan without circularity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office at a tax-advisory or virtual-office address with no physical presence in Quebec
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or serviced-office agreement with utility-bill corroboration; independent occupancy evidence; identification of an accountable Quebec-based financial officer or general-partner representative; and confirmation that the registered address is operational, not merely a mail-forwarding point.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 or, for intercompany funding, SWIFT MT202 for inbound equity contributions from the foreign parent into the Quebec LP’s Schedule 1 bank CAD or USD operational account. The wire must carry a Statistics Canada-compliant purpose code consistent with direct investment/equity capital and the remitter must provide, before or concurrently with the transfer, an executed equity subscription agreement, board/general-partner resolutions, source-of-funds evidence, and expected inflow/outflow narrative. Funds may be received in CAD, USD, EUR, CNY, HKD, or other convertible currencies and converted at the bank’s execution rate; all receipts are posted to the partnership capital-account ledger and made available to Revenu Québec and CRA for information verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements should clear through traditional interbank rails: SWIFT MT103 for straightforward supplier or distribution payments; Commercial Letters of Credit with presentation of conforming shipping and invoice documents for trade-backed obligations; and, for same-day CAD disbursements, Payments Canada’s Large-Value Transfer System (LVTS). USD payables should be settled through correspondent bank Fedwire or CHIPS clearing. All outbound wires must carry the appropriate cross-border payment purpose code and be supported by invoices, contractual milestones, or distribution resolutions to avoid FINTRAC, OSFI, and global-sanctions red flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR forward contracts executed with a Schedule 1 bank or licensed investment dealer
Cross-currency swaps matching medium-term CAD funding and foreign-currency dividend flows under an ISDA/CSA master agreement
OTC call/put FX options on CAD crosses where the counterparty is a regulated financial institution and prudent-rate/credit limits apply
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for less liquid emerging-market currency exposures with CAD or USD cash settlement, subject to counterparty-credit approval and OSFI prudential standards
Spot-locked FX execution trades with per-counterparty exposure limited to 10% of portfolio net asset value and same-day settlement through a tier-1 clearing bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the partnership's registration in the Quebec enterprise registry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Registrar may issue a default notice; failure to file the annual declaration for two consecutive anniversary periods exposes the limited partnership to administrative strike-off from the registry. Reinstatement requires filing of the missed declarations and payment of prescribed administrative fees; general partners remain responsible for obligations arising during the period of default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and related T5013 slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due on or before June 15 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of a required T5013 return is subject to a penalty of CAD 25 per day up to 100 days, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500. Late-filed T5013 slips attract a separate per-slip penalty of CAD 25 per day up to 100 days. Gross negligence penalties and prosecution provisions of the Income Tax Act (Canada) may also apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a Quebec limited partnership that is a passive equity-holding SPV; the Income Tax Act and Quebec registry legislation do not impose a revenue or asset-based audit threshold on unincorporated limited partnerships. An audit becomes mandatory only where required by the partnership agreement, a lender, an applicable regulatory statute, or where a partner is a reporting issuer or regulated financial entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private partnerships generally prepare financial statements under Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); IFRS may be elected where required by partners or financing arrangements. Partnership income allocation and tax reporting follow the Income Tax Act, including T5013 schedules and fiscal-period rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec limited partnerships are not share-capital corporations, so there is no annual shareholding declaration. The REQ annual declaration must confirm the identity of every general partner and the partnership's registered office and establishment data. Limited partner interests and transfers are recorded in the LP's internal register and reflected in the annual T5013 allocation. A public UBO declaration is not required solely because the entity is a société en commandite; if any partner is a reporting legal person under Quebec or federal transparency rules, the relevant significant-control register must be maintained and updated with the annual declaration cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners and Contributions
Minute Book of General Partner Resolutions and Consents
Original Limited Partnership Agreement and all amendments
Significant Control Register (UBO) where any partner is a reporting legal person or where a financing covenant requires transparency

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 180-450 (CAD 250-620) per year for a Quebec registered office or registered agent, depending on service scope and inclusion of annual declaration handling.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 7,000-18,000 for a voluntary certified audit of a simple holding LP; 3,000-6,500 for a review engagement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at LP level (fiscally transparent); corporate partners are taxed at the combined federal (15%) and Quebec (11.5%) general corporate rate of 26.5%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level income tax for the limited partnership; intercorporate dividend deduction for corporate partners (100% exemption for eligible dividends from taxable Canadian corporations); capital gains inclusion ratio of 50%; no small business deduction for passive investment income; no Quebec statutory tax holidays for holding SPVs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Summary, filed via CRA NETFILE/EFILE or My Business Account; T5013 slips issued to each partner
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: March 31 following the calendar-year end; for non-calendar fiscal period, the first day of the fifth month after the fiscal period end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nil for a pure equity-holding SPV unless commercial revenues are earned; non-resident partners' share of Canadian business income is subject to Part I tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital gains (losses) at 50% inclusion rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only 50% of capital gains realized on disposition of subsidiary shares. Non-resident partners may be exempt under DTA if gains relate to treaty-protected property and no permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends from taxable Canadian corporations (eligible dividends)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercorporate dividends are generally deductible to a corporate partner; for non-resident individual partners, Part XIII withholding may apply at source with treaty reduction.
Must be allocated to partners; interest paid to non-resident partners may attract Part XIII WHT unless treaty-reduced or exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net partnership income (loss) for allocation to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must file a Canadian T1/T2 return if the allocated income is from exercising a Canadian business; otherwise a T5013 slip suffices for reporting.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under s.162(7) ITA, late T5013 filing penalty is CAD 25 per day per partner for up to 100 partners, with a minimum CAD 100 after 31 days and maximum CAD 2,500. Failing to issue T5013 slips to partners attracts penalties of CAD 100 per slip. Repeated or false returns may trigger criminal penalties under s.239.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: TP-600 Questionnaire for a Partnership, filed via Revenu Québec's online business services (Mon dossier d'entreprise); RL-15 slips issued to partners
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: March 31 following the calendar-year end; if the fiscal period does not coincide with the calendar year, within five months after the fiscal period end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner identification and share of income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify each partner resident outside Canada; non-resident partners must provide treaty residency documentation to claim relief from Quebec withholding.
Income allocated from real property situated in Quebec or from a business carried on in Quebec is taxable in Quebec; non-residents must file a Quebec TP-1 or TP-2.
Quebec generally follows federal treatment; withholdings on dividends/interest paid to non-residents are governed by provincial rules aligning with Part XIII.
All expenses must be supported; a pure equity-holding SPV should have no substantial deductions other than professional fees and administrative costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day per partner up to 100 partners, minimum CAD 100 after 31 days. Failure to transmit RL-15 slips electronically attracts penalties of CAD 100 per slip up to CAD 5,000 per calendar year.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII ITA) on distributions out of Canada; reduced to 5% under most DTAs where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% voting shares; 15% portfolio rate for other shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident partner must file Form NR301 (Statutory Withholding Tax) and provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the home tax authority to the withholding agent before payment. In Quebec, a TP-1000 declaration and supporting documentation is required. The withholding agent retains the TRC and the tax authority may request it on audit; if not provided, a refund may be obtained by filing a Canadian tax return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 25%; treaty-reduced to 0% under the Canada-US treaty for arm's length interest paid to a US resident, or 10% for certain participative debt. Royalties: statutory 25%; treaty-reduced to 10% for trademarks/patents and 5% for copyright-related cultural rights under the Canada-US treaty; other DTAs vary.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 – the aggregate value of non-arm's length cross-border transactions with a particular non-resident related party requiring Form T106 (Reasonable Efforts Information Return). Master File and CbCR are mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated revenue exceeding CAD 1.1 billion (approx. EUR 750 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate Economic Substance Regulation; however, GAAR under s.245 ITA, treaty shopping restrictions, and the OECD Principal Purpose Test require real economic substance. A pure equity-holding LP must demonstrate commercial rationale, active management decisions, properly documented intercompany agreements, and adequate capitalization; otherwise dividends and gains may be recharacterized and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly misreporting partnership income, failing to disclose a foreign subsidiary, inflating deductible expenses, or hiding capital gains in the LP; facilitating tax evasion through sham transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under s.163(2) ITA equal to 50% of the understated tax; criminal fine under s.239(1) of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; Quebec also applies administrative penalties under s.1049 TLTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner may be jointly and severally liable for taxes, penalties, and interest if they authorized the fraud; travel bans may be issued under tax treaties; criminal imprisonment applies to responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and provide contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation when required; pricing intercompany services or share subscriptions without arm's length comparison; having no local file for capital transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment plus a 10% penalty on net adjustment (s.247(3)) if gross adjustment exceeds CAD 5 million or 10% of gross revenue; documentation penalty of CAD 1,000 per month for each failure. Interest accrues from the first non-compliance date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/partners who knowingly sign false documentation may face civil liability equal to the penalty portion; CRA can assess penalties against the partnership and collect from general partner assets; serious cases lead to criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Defaults on Non-Resident Partners
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making distributions of Canadian-source income/dividends to non-resident partners without deducting Part XIII or Part I withholding, failing to obtain TRC, or incorrectly claiming treaty relief without supporting certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agent is liable for the full unwithheld amount plus interest and penalties under s.227(8); penalty of 25% of the amount not withheld is imposed under s.227(3); repeated non-compliance can trigger prosecution under s.238(2).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Trust liability under s.227(3) applies to directors of the general partner; personal recovery includes seizure of personal assets and travel restrictions; if funds are intentionally diverted, personal criminal fines and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Quebec LP as a conduit to avoid Canadian tax on passive investment income, with no employees, offices, or decision-making capacity; structuring solely to obtain DTA benefits for the parent corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment under s.245(2) ITA denying the tax benefit and imposing interest and penalties; Quebec analog under s.1079.1 TLTA; monetary penalty of 50% of the tax benefit may be imposed if the arrangement was a planning misuse; treaty benefits may be denied under OECD BEPS PPT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: While GAAR is corporation-level, officers who knowingly implement a sham arrangement face joint personal liability for reassessed taxes and severe professional consequences; travel bans are possible in extreme cases; fraud charges may be brought under the Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a pure equity-holding SPV with opaque beneficial ownership, using the LP to layer dividends from sanctioned entities, or failing to register and report under PCMLTFA as a money services business if payments pass through.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 100,000 for individuals and CAD 500,000 for entities per violation under the PCMLTFA; criminal money laundering conviction carries imprisonment up to 14 years under s.462.31 of the Criminal Code; asset freeze and forfeiture orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly instruct, authorize, or participate in money laundering or financing of unlawful activities are personally liable to pay penalties and face imprisonment; travel bans and extradition are applicable under international instruments.
